class.name: FellowBurnable3D
class.brief_description: FellowEngine: makes a [MeshInstance3D] burn like wood: it chars, glows, recedes and ends as ash, its volatiles feeding the flames of a [FellowGasVolume3D].
class.description: The mesh of [member mesh_path] (empty: the parent) is voxelized ([member resolution] voxels along its longest side); each voxel has a temperature and how much of it is wood, char and ash. The GPU heats the voxels from the gas around the object (the flames' temperature, by convection and radiation) or from the surface's own flame (over the wood that is burning, climbing [member flame_reach] above it at [member flame_temperature]: what keeps the object burning on its own), conducts the heat inwards, pyrolyses the wood to char (above [member pyrolysis_temperature]; the volatiles become the gas's fuel, so the visible flames come from the object itself), oxidises the exposed char to ash (above [member glow_temperature]: glowing embers) and lets the remains (the ash, and the char where it has crumbled) fall to the ground below and slide into a heap, still glowing while hot. Once less than [member collapse_fraction] of the wood and char is left, the object's physics body stops colliding (signal [signal collapsed]). Thin parts burn through first, thick ones char slowly. The mesh is drawn from the voxels: its vertices recede with the material, its surface darkens with char and greys with ash, and the hot char glows in its cracks; where it has burned through it is not drawn, and the ash and the crumbled charcoal are drawn as a heap of their own (an internal child mesh instance, [code]FellowAshHeap[/code], added when the first ash appears). The gas flows around the object's voxels (its physics body is not the gas's obstacle). Runs only in a running game, not in the editor. While in the tree it replaces the mesh instance's mesh (subdivided so the surface can follow the voxels) and its materials ([BaseMaterial3D] and [ShaderMaterial] spatial shaders are extended with the burning); they are restored when it leaves. Needs a RenderingDevice renderer (Forward+ or Mobile). Without a gas volume an object lit by [method ignite] burns by its own flame, without visible flames. At most 8 burning objects inject into one gas volume. See [code]docs/decisions/0120-burning.md[/code].

method.name: get_ash_fraction
method.description: The share of the object's initial volume that is ash now (from the last readback, a few frames late).

method.name: get_burning_voxels
method.description: How many voxels are pyrolysing or glowing now.

method.name: get_char_fraction
method.description: The share of the object's initial volume that is char now.

method.name: get_debug_data
method.description: The data of the last [method request_debug_data], once [method is_debug_data_ready] (raw texels, for tests).

method.name: get_display_triangle_count
method.description: The triangles of the mesh drawn while burning (the original's, subdivided with [member subdivide]).

method.name: get_initial_fill
method.description: Each voxel's share inside the mesh when it was voxelized (0-1, X fastest), for tests.

method.name: get_last_step_info
method.description: The transforms and parameters of the last simulation step queued (for tests).

method.name: get_max_temperature
method.description: The hottest voxel's temperature in kelvin.

method.name: get_steps_simulated
method.description: The simulation steps run since the object was set up or reset.

method.name: get_voxel_grid_size
method.description: The voxel grid's size (from [member resolution] along the mesh's longest side).

method.name: get_voxel_origin
method.description: The voxel grid's corner in the mesh's space.

method.name: get_voxel_size
method.description: A voxel's edge in the mesh's units.

method.name: get_wood_fraction
method.description: The share of the object's initial volume that is still wood.

method.name: ignite
method.description: Heats the material within [param radius] metres of [param position] (global) to at least [param temperature] kelvin: lights the object without a gas volume's fire.

method.name: is_burned_out
method.description: [code]true[/code] once it has burned and nothing is burning or hot enough to pyrolyse any more (signal [signal burned_out]).

method.name: is_burning
method.description: [code]true[/code] while some voxel is pyrolysing or glowing.

method.name: is_collapsed
method.description: [code]true[/code] once less than [member collapse_fraction] of the wood and char is left and the physics body has stopped colliding (signal [signal collapsed]).

method.name: is_debug_data_ready
method.description: [code]true[/code] when the data of [method request_debug_data] has arrived.

method.name: request_debug_data
method.description: Reads a GPU state back asynchronously, for tests: [param what] 0 the voxels (RGBA32F: the temperature above the ambient, wood, char, ash), 1 the emission, 2 the injection into the gas. Poll [method is_debug_data_ready].

method.name: reset_burning
method.description: Starts again: the object set up anew from wood at the ambient temperature (its mesh, materials and physics body restored first).

members.member: The ash's colour, on the surface and in the heap.
The ash's volume as a share of the char it comes from (what is left in the heap).
Burning seconds per second: at 10 the wood burns ten times faster than real wood (the flames keep their real size).
The char's colour.
The share of the wood's mass that pyrolysis leaves as char (the rest are volatiles: the fuel).
With less of the wood and char than this left, the object's physics body stops colliding (its shapes disabled, a rigid body frozen) and [signal collapsed] is emitted.
The wood's thermal conductivity (W/(m K)): how fast heat goes inwards.
The size of the char's cracks (along the grain, the mesh's longest axis) where the embers glow.
The wood's density (kg/m³).
Draws the mesh burning (receding, charred, glowing); off, the simulation runs and the mesh is drawn as it was.
The share of the volatiles that burns where it is released (the flame attached to the surface, thinner than the gas's cells).
How much the fuel released flickers (the flames lick).
How far the surface's own flame climbs over the wood above it, in metres.
The fuel the volatiles give the gas (1: 2.7 of the gas's fuel units per kg): the visible flames' size.
The surface's own flame's temperature (kelvin): what keeps the object burning without the gas's flames; lower, it goes out by itself.
The [FellowGasVolume3D] whose fire heats the object and which its volatiles feed (empty: the volume holding the object's centre).
The embers' brightness.
How fast exposed char oxidises to ash above [member glow_temperature], per second.
Char glows and turns to ash above this (kelvin).
The [MeshInstance3D] that burns (empty: the parent).
How fast wood above [member pyrolysis_temperature] turns to char and volatiles, per second.
Wood pyrolyses above this (kelvin).
Voxels along the mesh's longest side.
Off: the burning stops where it is (no steps).
Smoke released with the volatiles, per unit of fuel.
The wood's specific heat (J/(kg K)).
Subdivides the drawn mesh to about 1.5 voxels per edge, so the surface can follow the voxels as it recedes.
How fast a hot surface heats the air next to it, per second.

signal.name: burned_out
signal.description: Emitted once when the object has burned and nothing is burning any more.

signal.name: collapsed
signal.description: Emitted once when the object's physics body stops colliding ([member collapse_fraction]).

signal.name: ignited
signal.description: Emitted once when the first voxel starts burning.
